text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The U.S. ambassador to Zambia, Arlene Render, said the United States would oppose plans by Frederick Chiluba's government to set up a statutory media council.
- Minister without portfolio Michael Sata criticised the United States for taking a hard-line stance on Zambia, even though the country had adopted high democratic standards.
- The supreme court ordered that the editor of the state-run Times of Zambia be prosecuted for contempt over reports alleging that witnesses in a presidential electoral legal suit were bribed.
- The cash-strapped government has failed to pay public health workers their March salaries.
- The federation of the blind urged the government to drop plans to repatriate blind people in urban areas to their home villages.
